### TAG-225: `Emitter: contained dispatch cases shouldn't emit standalone entities`

**Status:** ⬜ Not started

## Software Notes

## Software notes

When a definition has composed-dispatch cases inside its \`def.contained\` (the \`A\[out1< $in >\]\`, \`B\[out2< $in >\]\` rows under a \`$select() :\` header), the emitter currently treats each contained entry as a full \`network.Definition\` and emits a standalone entity + architecture for it. Those entities are malformed: they have no ports, because the entry's own \`sources\` and \`destinations\` lists are empty, but their architecture bodies reference the places named inside the fill (\`out1\`, \`ms_in\`), which were never declared as ports.

Reproduced with TAG-147's \`fanout\`:

fanout\[ (select<> input<>)({$out1 $out2 $out3 $out4 $out5})
   $select( ) :  A\[out1< $in >\]
                 B\[out2< $in >\]
                 C\[out3< $in >\]
                 D\[out4< $in >\]
\]

```
The emitter produces, in `.verify_scratch/TAG-147-example-12.13.ms.ipl.vhd`:
```vhdl
entity fanout_a is
end fanout_a;
architecture rtl of fanout_a is
  signal complete   : std_logic;
  signal out1 : ncl_signal;
  signal ms_in : ncl_signal;
begin
  complete <= '1';
  out1 <= ms_in;
end rtl;
```

The entity has no `port(...)` clause; the architecture declares `out1` and `ms_in` as internal signals and asserts them, but nothing drives or reads them. Same shape for `fanout_b`, `fanout_c`, `fanout_d` and `fanin_a`, `fanin_b`. GHDL accepts the file because these are structurally valid VHDL, but they're dead entities — nothing instantiates them, and they don't correspond to any behavior the parent definition actually needs emitted.

## Why they're being emitted

The composed-dispatch cases in `def.contained` are the *branches* of the dispatch, not separate definitions. The runtime already treats them correctly — `rules.appendSelectRules` builds one `.select` rule per destination place, with entries keyed by the case name (`A`, `B`, `C`, `D`). The emitter's dispatch path (`writeTransformRules` / the `.select` emission in `network_entity.zig`) likewise handles them as inline cases, matching the `$select()` dispatch at the parent level.
But the top-level emission loop in `network_entity.zig` still walks every contained entry as if it were a nested definition:

```zig
// 1. Write children/contained definitions first (so they are declared
//    before instantiation)
for (def.contained) |contained| {
    if (contained.name.len == 0 or std.ascii.isDigit(contained.name[0])) continue;
    if (value_transform_analysis.isValueTransformRule(contained)) continue;
    try writer.print("\n", .{});
    const child_scope = try invocation.scopedDefinitionName(allocator, def_id, contained.name);
    defer allocator.free(child_scope);
    try writeDefinition(allocator, writer, contained, def_id, top);
}
```

The `isValueTransformRule` guard skips value-transform rules (like `K[SUM<K>]`). It does **not** skip composed-dispatch cases like `A[out1< $in >]`, because those have a different shape: name is `A`, no sources, no destinations, resolution is a single `.fill` (not a `.pure_value`). So `writeDefinition` is called on them, and the emitter's port-emission path sees zero boundary ports and emits an empty entity.

## What the fix looks like

The composed-dispatch cases should be skipped in the top-level emission loop, the same way value-transform rules are. They're already handled inline by the parent's dispatch emission; emitting them as standalone entities is redundant and produces dead VHDL.
Two possible conditions for the guard:
**Option A — match the dispatch shape directly.** Skip any contained entry whose resolution is a single `.fill` (which is what `A[out1< $in >]` produces), or whose parent uses a composed-dispatch header. The parent's header is the reliable signal: if `findComposedDispatchHeader(def) != null`, all `.fill`-shaped contained entries are dispatch cases, not nested definitions.
**Option B — reuse the check the runtime already uses.** The runtime's `appendSelectRules` iterates `def.contained` and collects entries with `sources.len == 0 and destinations.len == 0` and resolution `.fill`. Anything matching that shape under a dispatch header is a dispatch case. The emitter can use the same predicate.
Option A is simpler: gate the child-emission loop on `findComposedDispatchHeader(def) == null`. When the parent is a composed dispatch, its contained entries are handled inline and should not be emitted as entities.

## Acceptance criteria

* TAG-147's emitted VHDL contains no `entity fanout_a`, `entity fanout_b`, `entity fanout_c`, `entity fanout_d`, `entity fanin_a`, or `entity fanin_b`.
* `entity fanout` and `entity fanin` still emit with their correct ports (`ms_select`, `input`, `out1..out5`; `ms_select`, `in1`, `in2`, `ms_out`).
* Every currently-passing example stays passing: `zig build verify` shows no regression on the GHDL column.
* No change to runtime behavior — the runtime already handled these correctly; this is an emitter-only fix.

## Scope notes

* This is independent of the runtime's `appendSelectRules` behavior and of the `.pure_value`-vs-`.fill` distinction in `def.contained`. It's a pure emitter cleanup.
* The empty `entity fanout_a is end fanout_a;` declarations are what happens when `boundary.boundaryCount(def.sources) + boundary.boundaryCount(def.destinations) == 0` in `writeEntityHeader`. That path is *correct* for genuinely portless definitions (constants, value-transform rules), but wrong for dispatch cases that were never meant to be standalone entities at all.
* An alternative fix would be to give the dispatch-case entities proper ports (their fill's `dest_name` and any `$name` references). But that would require the emitter to reason about what a case's ports are, which is a much larger change and not what the dispatch path needs — the parent handles the case inline, so the child entity serves no purpose.

```

A couple of notes before filing:

**The condition to gate on.** I'd use `findComposedDispatchHeader(def) == null` (or the equivalent in the emitter — it's currently only in `rules.zig`, but `syntax.zig` has the shape check). If it's null, walk `def.contained` as before. If it's non-null, skip the walk entirely — the dispatch path handles everything inline. That's simpler than per-entry classification and matches the semantic ("a definition with a dispatch header has no independently-emittable children").

**Whether the entities are actually dead.** I'm assuming no instantiations reference them, based on the emitted VHDL you pasted (`fanout_network` instantiates `work.fanout`, not `work.fanout_a`). If something *does* instantiate them, the fix is different — you'd need to give them ports instead of skipping them. Worth a grep for `work.fanout_a` or `fanout_a` in the emitted file to confirm before committing to the "skip" fix.
